topic: Probability-weighted Fourier exposure-incidence minimax frontier for off-policy causal estimation in networks.

open_problems.open_problem: Is the finite linear-minimax risk F over assignment-indexed weights and bounded local-Fourier evaluation polytopes universally comparable to unrestricted all-measurable-estimator minimax MSE under one product-Bernoulli network experiment?

source_refs.claim: The paper derives the unique minimum-L2 unbiased Fourier transport weight and a sufficient consistency bound, but does not compare its risk with unrestricted measurable-estimator minimax risk.
source_refs.author: Sahil Loomba and Dean Eckles

source_refs.claim: For Gaussian sequence estimation over orthosymmetric quadratically convex sets, linear minimax risk is within a universal factor of unrestricted minimax risk, while the comparison can fail outside that geometry.
source_refs.author: David L. Donoho, Richard C. Liu, and Brenda MacGibbon

source_refs.excerpt: Future work includes the exact leading constant for the all-measurable-estimator minimax risk
Make the lower-bound handle explicitly fuzzy: specify two block-schedule priors (or an Assouad cube)

open_problems.why_unsolved: The web anchor solves the linear unbiased transport problem, while the accepted SNIPE proposal leaves the unrestricted-estimator constant open. Here all unit outcomes are observed at one common assignment, so overlapping Fourier supports couple the bounded schedules; this is neither an i.i.d. off-policy experiment nor an additive Gaussian sequence model. The linear moment dual can therefore yield a signed measure that is not a probability law on genuine bounded schedules, and deterministic alternatives may become singular after one informative assignment. New work must replace the complete-block scalar Hellinger calculation by a dimension-free, structure-preserving prior-rounding or posterior-ambiguity lemma.
open_problems.what_a_resolution_would_look_like: A resolution would give universal constants c,C>0 with cF <= R_all^* <= CF for every admissible graph, positive source-target policy pair, support family, and outcome bound, plus a clipped incidence estimator for the upper bound and genuine bounded-schedule priors for the lower bound.

writing_exemplar.why: Its motivation, policy-transport setup, and biased-Fourier formulation are the closest framing; the new paper would turn its estimator-side geometry into an unrestricted minimax benchmark.
writing_exemplar.motivation_arc: Network causal values depend on the assignment policy -> global importance weighting is unstable -> local Fourier structure yields exact transport weights -> bounded schedules demand a benchmark against every measurable estimator

method_exemplars.technique: Compare nonlinear and linear minimax risks through hard finite-dimensional subproblems and a universal convex-geometric constant.
method_exemplars.why_closest: The bounded Fourier evaluation sets are finite convex bodies, so a structure-preserving analogue of the linear-versus-unrestricted comparison is the nearest proof template for cF <= R_all^*.

method_exemplars.technique: Reduce design-based minimax risk over arbitrary estimators to graph-indexed observation conflicts and prove matching upper and lower bounds.
method_exemplars.why_closest: It supplies the procedure-agnostic one-assignment network decision framework; the proposed resolution must refine its conflict geometry with the source-target Fourier moment body.

open_problems.open_problem: Does bounded treewidth of the bipartite exposure-incidence graph yield exact computation of F, rather than merely a compact factorization of the source policy and local Fourier constraints?

source_refs.claim: The Fourier transport formulas factor over product-Bernoulli assignments and local supports, but the paper does not formulate or solve the bounded-outcome finite minimax program.
source_refs.author: Sahil Loomba and Dean Eckles

source_refs.claim: Treewidth-indexed Sherali-Adams and Lasserre relaxations are exact for appropriate binary graphical-model moment polytopes.
source_refs.author: Martin J. Wainwright and Michael I. Jordan

source_refs.excerpt: polynomial-time computation and compressed graph summaries remain open
Develop a bounded-degree or bounded-exposure-incidence compression theorem with an explicit algorithm

open_problems.why_unsolved: Product Bernoulli probabilities and local Fourier evaluation constraints factor, but the supremum over bounded schedules, the square of the global bias, and the dual moment body can create fill-in across distant bags. The prior finite-saddle proposal remains exponential and only compresses when symmetries are supplied. Generic junction-tree or hierarchy theorems become relevant only after proving that separator states preserve every global estimator-weight and schedule-moment constraint; otherwise incidence treewidth controls the input description but not the optimizer.
open_problems.what_a_resolution_would_look_like: A resolution would define the optimizer-relevant incidence graph, give a poly(n)exp(O(tw)) exact dynamic program or extended formulation with liftable optimal weights and dual certificates, prove disjoint-motif factorization, and give convergent certified primal-dual bounds or a hardness theorem for general graphs.

writing_exemplar.why: Its local Fourier support formulation makes the statistical optimization concrete while leaving the computational boundary untouched.
writing_exemplar.motivation_arc: Fourier locality compresses policy transport -> overlapping neighborhoods define a sparse incidence graph -> finite minimax risk still requires a global optimizer -> treewidth may delimit exact risk certification

method_exemplars.technique: Lift binary polynomial constraints to local moments and prove collapse of a treewidth-indexed Sherali-Adams or Lasserre level to the global moment polytope.
method_exemplars.why_closest: The dual of F is a finite moment-consistency problem, so hierarchy collapse is the closest mechanism for certifying exactness at bounded incidence width.

method_exemplars.technique: Eliminate variables along a tree decomposition while storing exact separator messages with state size exponential only in bag width.
method_exemplars.why_closest: If squared minimax risk closes under local moments, separator messages can carry the optimizer; proving that closure is exactly the first missing step.

open_problems.open_problem: Can consistency of off-policy network-value estimation be characterized by F_n -> 0 if and only if unrestricted minimax MSE vanishes, with a genuinely overlapping growing family on which F is strictly sharper than the anchor's B(D+1)/n envelope?

source_refs.claim: The paper proves consistency from a sufficient bound based on intersecting influence sets and uniform covariance control, leaving necessity and an exact frontier open.
source_refs.author: Sahil Loomba and Dean Eckles

source_refs.claim: The design-based Riesz framework gives necessary and sufficient conditions for unbiasedness and consistency of Riesz estimators for linear functionals over specified potential-outcome spaces.
source_refs.author: Christopher Harshaw, Fredrik Savje, and Yitan Wang

source_refs.claim: Under Bernoulli assignment and low-order neighborhood interactions, the paper gives the SNIPE estimator, variance control, a minimax lower bound, and asymptotic normality for the all-treated-versus-all-control target.
source_refs.author: Mayleen Cortez-Rodriguez, Matthew Eichhorn, and Christina Lee Yu

source_refs.excerpt: Strengthen the lower-bound question beyond block compression by proving a graph-family frontier

open_problems.why_unsolved: The anchor's B(D+1)/n calculation records only whether influence neighborhoods intersect and replaces every nonzero covariance by one worst-case magnitude, discarding source-cell probabilities, heterogeneous policy shifts, signs, cancellations, and motif repetition. Existing Riesz criteria concern a restricted representer class, while the prior lower bounds tensorize disjoint complete blocks and therefore cannot show whether graph overlap and positivity penalties are separately necessary. The first lower-bound step must change from a product block-distance calculation to an overlap-aware genuine-prior coupling, while the upper side must retain the signed probability-weighted incidence geometry.
open_problems.what_a_resolution_would_look_like: A resolution would prove R_all,n^* -> 0 iff F_n -> 0, exhibit an explicit path, star, hub, or overlapping repeated-motif sequence with F_n=o(B_n(D_n+1)/n), give a matching unrestricted lower bound on that family, and recover the exact disjoint-motif formula as a special case.

writing_exemplar.why: Its narrative moves from expressive causal functionals to representer geometry and then to necessary-and-sufficient estimability conditions, the right arc for an iff frontier.
writing_exemplar.motivation_arc: Interference creates many design-based linear targets -> function spaces encode admissible schedules -> representer geometry governs estimability -> exact probability-weighted incidence geometry should govern consistency

method_exemplars.technique: Construct low-order Bernoulli Fourier scores and control variance by covariance counting over intersecting neighborhoods.
method_exemplars.why_closest: Its interaction model is a downward-closed local Fourier support, so its score and lower-bound witnesses are the nearest starting points for the exact probability-weighted incidence frontier.

method_exemplars.technique: Analyze unrestricted design-based minimax risk through a graph-dependent finite decision problem rather than through one estimator's variance.
method_exemplars.why_closest: It provides the procedure-agnostic benchmark needed to certify that the strict improvement of F over a degree envelope is intrinsic rather than estimator-specific.

open_problems.open_problem: Under what primitive weighted-incidence and Fourier-influence conditions is the clipped minimax incidence estimator asymptotically normal and studentizable with honest design-based coverage from one assignment?

source_refs.claim: The paper states an abstract Doob-martingale CLT and identifiable variance bounds, but does not derive primitive conditions tailored to minimax-selected clipped weights.
source_refs.author: Sahil Loomba and Dean Eckles

source_refs.claim: Under approximate neighborhood interference and topology restrictions, inverse-probability estimators are consistent and asymptotically normal with a conservative network-HAC variance estimator.
source_refs.author: Michael P. Leung

source_refs.claim: The paper characterizes admissible estimable quadratic variance upper bounds under interference and computes minimally conservative bounds by convex optimization.
source_refs.author: Christopher Harshaw, Joel Middleton, and Fredrik Savje
source_refs.venue: Journal of the American Statistical Association

source_refs.excerpt: Variance estimation, studentization, and limit-law theory are outside the present theorem scope.
a design-based Horvitz-Thompson CLT and oracle Wald coverage

open_problems.why_unsolved: The anchor's martingale hypotheses depend on estimator-specific Doob differences and quadratic variation rather than observable graph primitives. Minimax weights can be heterogeneous, clipping adds bias that must be negligible relative to the standard error, and Fourier cancellations can make first-order variance degenerate. The prior ego-cluster proof handles an unclipped Horvitz-Thompson contrast under explicit nondegeneracy, while network-HAC and optimized variance-bound results do not establish uniform coverage for weights chosen by the finite minimax program.
open_problems.what_a_resolution_would_look_like: A resolution would state checkable probability-weighted incidence and Fourier-influence assumptions implying a martingale or dependency-graph CLT, prove clipping bias is o(standard error), and construct an observable conservative variance estimator whose studentized interval has uniform asymptotic coverage at least 1-alpha, with a separate degenerate-direction result.

writing_exemplar.why: It explicitly sets up the gap between the Fourier off-policy estimator, an abstract Doob CLT, and usable design-based uncertainty quantification.
writing_exemplar.motivation_arc: Fourier transport yields a point estimator -> one assignment creates network dependence and unidentified covariance -> an abstract martingale limit is available -> primitive conditions and observable studentization remain missing

method_exemplars.technique: Translate interference decay and graph topology into asymptotic normality and conservative network-HAC variance control.
method_exemplars.why_closest: Both problems turn local network dependence into a limit law, but the new proof must use probability-weighted Fourier incidence and control clipping bias.

method_exemplars.technique: Optimize over estimable quadratic upper bounds for an unidentified design-based variance while retaining finite-population conservativeness.
method_exemplars.why_closest: The clipped incidence estimator also has unidentified cross-potential-outcome covariance, making this convex bound machinery the nearest route to reportable standard errors.

open_problems.open_problem: How should the source product-Bernoulli design be chosen to minimize the worst-case probability-weighted incidence frontier over an entire target-policy curve rather than at one target policy?

source_refs.claim: The discussion identifies integrated or worst-case risk over a target-policy path and experimental design for an entire policy curve as open directions.
source_refs.author: Sahil Loomba and Dean Eckles

source_refs.claim: The paper evaluates stochastic seeding policies off-policy and studies experimental designs that improve precision for comparisons between seeding strategies.
source_refs.author: Alex Chin, Dean Eckles, and Johan Ugander

source_refs.claim: The paper derives minimax-variance experimental designs from an explicit structural outcome-function class and connects balance restrictions to worst-case precision.
source_refs.author: Nathan Kallus
source_refs.venue: Journal of the Royal Statistical Society, Series B

open_problems.why_unsolved: The source probabilities alter the biased Fourier basis, all source-target evaluation coefficients, and the overlap covariance geometry simultaneously, so convexity of F in estimator weights does not imply convexity of the outer design problem. A design optimized for one target can leave another saturation or seeding policy nearly unsupported. Existing stochastic-seeding and minimax-balance designs do not optimize the bounded local-Fourier network frontier uniformly over a target set.
open_problems.what_a_resolution_would_look_like: A resolution would characterize or compute a positive source policy pi_star minimizing sup_{pi_prime in Q} F(pi,pi_prime), or its integrated analogue, under budget constraints, prove an exact or approximation guarantee, and state necessary and sufficient conditions for one design to support the full target-policy curve consistently.

writing_exemplar.why: It motivates comparison of multiple stochastic network policies and connects off-policy evaluation directly to experiment design and seeding applications.
writing_exemplar.motivation_arc: Many stochastic seeding policies are scientifically plausible -> dedicated pairwise experiments are costly -> off-policy reuse compares policies -> the source design should insure precision over the whole policy class

method_exemplars.technique: Formulate design as worst-case variance minimization over a structured outcome class and solve the resulting balance problem with exact or semidefinite optimization.
method_exemplars.why_closest: The finite Fourier-support class is the network analogue of the structured response class, while F supplies the exact robust-design objective.

method_exemplars.technique: Use design-aware importance sampling and optimize experiments for contrasts among stochastic seeding policies.
method_exemplars.why_closest: Its target is already a collection of network policy values; the new proof would replace global likelihood-ratio variance with the exact local Fourier-incidence frontier.

literature_map:
Loomba and Eckles (2026, arXiv:2609.02756) is the exact anchor: biased-Fourier transport under heterogeneous Bernoulli policies, structured chi-square distance, a sufficient overlap condition, conservative variance bounds, and an abstract Doob CLT.
Harshaw, Savje, and Wang (2022, arXiv:2210.08698) place design-based causal functionals in Riesz geometry and provide necessary/sufficient estimability and consistency conditions, but not bounded-outcome unrestricted minimax risk.
Cortez-Rodriguez, Eichhorn, and Yu (2023, JCI, DOI 10.1515/jci-2022-0051) study Bernoulli network experiments with low-order neighborhood interactions, giving the SNIPE estimator, a minimax lower bound, and a CLT.
Aronow and Samii (2017, AOAS, DOI 10.1214/16-AOAS1005) supply the foundational exposure-mapping/IPW framework and design-based asymptotics under local dependence.
Savje (2024, Biometrika, DOI 10.1093/biomet/asad019) separates exposure definitions from interference assumptions and gives consistency under weakly dependent misspecification errors.
Leung (2022, Econometrica, DOI 10.3982/ECTA17841) replaces exact neighborhood interference by distance decay and obtains IPW asymptotics with network-HAC inference.
Chin, Eckles, and Ugander (2022, Management Science, DOI 10.1287/mnsc.2021.3963) evaluate stochastic seeding strategies off-policy and connect importance weighting to network experiment design.
Yu, Airoldi, Borgs, and Chayes (2022, PNAS, DOI 10.1073/pnas.2208975119) show that additive structure or baseline information can rescue total-effect estimation when the network is unknown.
Jagadeesan, Pillai, and Volfovsky (2020, AOS, DOI 10.1214/18-AOS1807) and Cortez-Rodriguez, Eichhorn, and Yu (2025, AISTATS) provide correlated designs that expose the limits of product-space Fourier lifts.
Wang, Agarwal, and Dudik (2017, ICML) and Ma, Zhu, Jiao, and Wainwright (2022, IEEE TIT) prove finite-sample minimax OPE and clipping phenomena for i.i.d. bandit data, not one-assignment network schedules.
Donoho, Liu, and MacGibbon (1990) and Donoho (1994) give linear-versus-nonlinear minimax comparisons in Gaussian convex models; the missing bridge is a genuine prior respecting bounded network schedules.
Wainwright and Jordan (2004/2008) and Peyrard et al. (2019) connect local moment polytopes and exact computation to treewidth; no located paper proves that the off-policy minimax optimizer inherits this locality.
Kandiros, Harshaw, and Savje (2026, arXiv:2608.04909) characterize unrestricted design-based network minimax risk through conflict graphs, but do not incorporate heterogeneous-policy Fourier transport.
Harshaw, Middleton, and Savje (2026, JASA, DOI 10.1080/01621459.2026.2627027) optimize conservative variance bounds under interference, complementing the point-risk frontier.
Crepon et al. (2013, QJE, DOI 10.1093/qje/qjt001) and the Chin-Eckles-Ugander seeding studies supply application regimes where exact incidence certificates could reveal design mismatch hidden by degree bounds.
